title: Benchmark: 500 x 220 nm silicon strip modes (published n_eff, n_g)
description:
Benchmark against published values (not a closed form): the quasi-TE0 mode of the standard 500 x 220 nm silicon strip fully clad in silica at 1550 nm, the most quoted silicon-photonics waveguide. Commonly published (e.g. Chrostowski and Hochberg, Silicon Photonics Design; commercial mode solvers with dispersive silicon): n_eff about 2.44, group index about 4.2. These carry the references of n_eff_TE0 and n_g_TE0; the published numbers themselves scatter by about 0.01 (n_eff) and 0.05 (n_g) with the material data and solver used, so read the agreement as roughly 1% in n_eff and 2-3% in n_g, not as an exact test.
Quarter domain: the strip is symmetric about both axes, so x min is an antisymmetric mirror (keeps E_x even in x) and y min a symmetric mirror (E_x even in y): only the quasi-TE family is solved, on a quarter of the unknowns. The mirror planes lie on the domain edges x = 0 and y = 0 (their ghost cells are added outside), so the quarter core spans 0 to w_core/2 and 0 to h_core/2. For quasi-TM0 swap the mirrors (x min symmetric, y min antisymmetric); n_eff about 1.7-1.8 is then expected (no reference given).
Materials: silicon is dispersive here, unlike the library silicon: permittivity 1 plus a lossless Lorentz pole equal to the first term of Li's Sellmeier fit (strength 10.668 at 301.5 nm: n = 3.477 at 1550 nm, bulk group index about 3.6), so the group index includes the material dispersion, as the published values do. Set si_dispersion = 0 for a constant index (eps = its 1550 nm value): n_eff stays, n_g drops by roughly 0.1. Silica is the library constant n = 1.444 (its own dispersion would add only about 0.01 to n_g).
Study: mode_analysis at lambda0 with Compute group index on, swept over dx_cell = 10 and 5 nm (a mesh-convergence check; a value must divide 110 nm and 250 nm so the core faces lie on cell edges): about 4.5e4 and 1.6e5 unknowns. Derived values tab: n_eff_TE0 and n_g_TE0 with reference and relative error per run; Sweep tab: both vs dx_cell with the references dashed. The arithmetic face averaging of the permittivity converges to first order in dx, so 5 nm should sit closer to the references than 10 nm and 2 n(5 nm) - n(10 nm) estimates the converged value. te_fraction_TE0 is close to 1. A second table row, if any, is a cladding mode with n_eff below 1.444.
Parameters to change: w_core, h_core (keep them multiples of 2 dx_cell), lambda0, si_dispersion.
